SaaS really dying, or is AI completely changing how software businesses are built and sold?

Today, anyone can use AI coding tools to build applications, websites, and SaaS products faster than ever.

But here's the BIG question:

If everyone can build software, who is going to buy your application?

During my consulting sessions, one question keeps coming up:

"Bro, I've built an application. How do I market it? How do I get customers? How do I actually sell it?"

That's exactly what we're discussing in this video.

Building software is becoming easier. Getting customers is still the real challenge!

In this video, I'll explain the changing SaaS landscape, the importance of understanding market trends, and why marketing, distribution, and customer acquisition matter more than ever for AI builders and startup founders.

What You'll Learn

•  Is SaaS really dead in the AI era?

•  How AI coding tools are changing software development

•  Why building an application doesn't guarantee sales

•  How to identify market trends and customer demand

•  The importance of product positioning and distribution

•  How to think about marketing your SaaS application

•  How to identify your ideal customers

•  Why some AI-built products struggle to attract buyers

•  The difference between building software and building a business

•  Practical lessons for AI app builders, founders, and indie hackers

AI Is Changing the SaaS Industry

With AI powered coding tools, developers and entrepreneurs can create applications more quickly.

But faster development also means more products competing for attention.

That's why understanding your customers, identifying real problems, and building an effective distribution strategy are essential.

The question is no longer just "Can you build it?"

The bigger question is "Can you find customers who need it?"

How Do You Market and Sell Your SaaS?

If you've already built an application but don't know how to market it, this video is for you.

We'll explore how to approach market research, identify customer problems, understand current trends, and think about getting your first paying customers.

Whether you're building an AI application, micro-SaaS, automation tool, or traditional SaaS product, these business fundamentals matter.

videos.title: Ramp’s Bet on the 100x Employee
videos.description:
Ramp started with a simple promise: help companies save time and money. Seven years later, it’s a $60 billion platform running the financial operations of tens of thousands of businesses, with more than $2 billion in annual revenue. Now, Ramp is using AI not just inside its products, but to rethink how the company itself works. On this episode of How to Build the Future, Ramp co-founder and CEO joins YC's Garry Tan to talk about the company’s journey from its earliest days and how AI has made some people at Ramp radically more productive. That shift led Ramp to rethink how work gets done across the organization, and Eric believes it could eventually let even large companies move with the speed of startups again.

videos.title: Senator Bernie Sanders: Iran Wasn't Trump's Idea. Someone Else Pushed Him Into It!
videos.description:
Can America's democracy still be saved at the ballot box, or has big money already bought the outcome? Senator Bernie Sanders joins to lay out what it will take to save American democracy, working families and the future of the Democratic Party.

Senator Bernie Sanders is the longest-serving independent in U.S. congressional history and a two-time presidential candidate who ignited a modern political revolution. Through his bestselling book _It's OK to Be Angry About Capitalism_ and national tours against oligarchy, he leads the charge to restore power to the working class. His ongoing movement challenges entrenched political and corporate monopolies to prove that government must serve human needs over billionaire profits.

*In this episode, he explains:*
*■ Legalized Oligarchy:* Campaign finance rules and corporate lobbying have replaced democratic deliberation with a “pay to play” structure where elite donors quietly draft national policy behind closed doors.
*■ The Incrementalism Trap:* Demanding minor, safe policy compromises alienates struggling voters and drives disillusioned working class communities straight into the arms of authoritarian leaders.
*■ Unregulated Automation:* Handing unchecked artificial intelligence development over to private tech oligarchs will trigger catastrophic white collar and manual job losses without shared public oversight.
*■ Systemic Wealth Hoarding:* Imposing a targeted wealth tax and closing tax free borrowing loopholes on unrealized equity is essential to halt the multi trillion dollar wealth siphon bleeding working class households.
*■ Universal Basic Dignity:* Establishing nonnegotiable guarantees like Medicare for All permanently breaks the psychological chokehold corporate employers hold over an anxious, underinsured workforce.

videos.title: Give Me 18 Minutes and You'll Finally Let Go
videos.description:
Most of us already know when something isn't working. The hard part is not starting over. It's letting go.

In this episode, Jay Shetty talks about why we hold on to relationships, jobs and dreams we have already outgrown. He explains the bias that makes a loss feel about twice as strong as an equal gain, and the trap that keeps us paying for years we have already spent.

He shares the one question that removes nostalgia from a hard decision, and why what we really hold on to is often the person we got to be inside a situation, not the situation itself.

And he talks about the hidden cost of staying, what research on regret says we regret most over time, and why a feeling is not an instruction.

Learn why your brain protects a life you no longer want. And learn the question to ask before you stay in anything.
